key_insight: A speech-based multimodal LLM framework that combines audio and transcript features can improve cognitive impairment detection and generalize better than single-modality approaches.
clinical_relevance: This suggests a non-invasive, privacy-preserving screening tool that may support earlier identification of cognitive impairment in diverse clinical settings.
method: Extract acoustic embeddings directly from speech audio.
Generate textual embeddings from automatic speech transcripts.
Concatenate both modality-specific embeddings for downstream classification using open-source LLMs.
evidence_signal: The model was evaluated on ADReSS20 and ADReSSo21 benchmarks and achieved 92.4% classification accuracy, outperforming single-modality baselines and showing stronger cross-dataset generalization.
watch_item: Performance may depend on transcript quality and benchmark-specific conditions, so real-world robustness across accents, devices, and clinical workflows still needs validation.
paper_title: Toward Generalizable Cognitive Impairment Detection with Speech-Based Multimodal Large Language Models
